answer: An economy of AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance through cryptographic staking tied to verifiable hardware enclaves, rendering any unbacked identity hollow. When an agent attempts to flood the network with fake peers, isolation protocols treat the cluster as an untrusted island that cannot route transactions. To bypass this, an attacker must pay a prohibitive computational signal tax in scarce tokens per node, making large-scale spoofing economically irrational.
